Overview

Stuttgart as a Business Centre

Stuttgart is the capital of Baden-Württemberg and the centre of one of Europe's most industrialised regions. More than 29,000 companies are based in the city, generating over 308 billion euros in revenue in 2022, and its gross value added of 53 billion euros was slightly over a tenth of the state total. Mercedes-Benz and Porsche are headquartered there, alongside the engine and thermal systems group Mahle, construction group Ed. Züblin, testing organisation DEKRA and pharmaceutical wholesalers. About 538,000 people worked in the city in 2022, nearly 15 percent in manufacturing, and more than 60 percent of employees commute in from the surrounding region of engineering and machinery firms.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Stuttgart because the automotive and engineering economy is going through a costly transition to electric drivetrains and software. Typical triggers include due diligence on suppliers and family-owned Mittelstand companies being bought, refinanced or restructured; research on counterparties and new owners after distressed sales; support to counsel in post-acquisition, shareholder and management liability disputes, which since 2025 can be heard by an English-capable Commercial Court in Stuttgart; and inquiries into suspected leaks of engineering know-how to competitors. Procurement fraud, supplier conflicts of interest and export control questions involving machinery and components also arise.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Stuttgart

01

Automotive supplier due diligence

Research on suppliers in the Stuttgart region ahead of sourcing, acquisition or refinancing decisions, covering commercial register filings, published accounts, insolvency announcements, ownership changes and litigation, to identify financial distress, undisclosed related parties and dependence on a single vehicle manufacturer.

02

Mittelstand acquisition background research

Background on family-owned engineering and machinery companies and their owners and managers before acquisition or investment, mapping shareholdings, holding structures, succession arrangements and reputational history, so buyers and investors understand who controls the business and what disputes may follow a sale.

03

Shareholder and management dispute support

Fact development for counsel in disputes over company acquisitions, share purchases and claims against managing directors or supervisory board members, areas assigned to the Stuttgart Commercial Court, including chronology work, party background and lawful asset research for enforcement.

04

Trade secret and know-how leakage

Support to counsel and internal teams where engineering data, designs or customer information may have reached a competitor, focusing on corporate links between departing employees, new ventures and suppliers, within German employee data protection rules and works council arrangements.

05

Distressed counterparty and restructuring research

Research on buyers, investors and service providers emerging in restructurings of Stuttgart-area suppliers, testing their track record, ownership and source of funds, to help creditors, customers and administrators judge whether proposed rescuers are credible and appropriately independent.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Stuttgart

Stuttgart Commercial Court

Under the federal Commercial Courts Act in force since 1 April 2025, Baden-Württemberg established a Commercial Court at the Higher Regional Court Stuttgart and Commercial Chambers at the Regional Court Stuttgart. Proceedings can be conducted in German or English. The Commercial Court takes business-to-business disputes of at least 500,000 euros in company law, including disputes over acquiring a company or at least 3 percent of its shares and claims between a company and its management or supervisory board.

Earlier English-capable chambers

Baden-Württemberg was an early mover: since 1 November 2020 specialised commercial chambers at the Regional Courts in Stuttgart and Mannheim have heard larger international commercial disputes with judges experienced in English, although pleadings and judgments then remained in German. The 2025 framework extends this, and Commercial Chambers in Stuttgart may now take qualifying cases from a value of 10,000 euros. Counsel decides which forum suits a claim.

Courts and commercial register

The Regional Court Stuttgart hears commercial and corporate litigation for the city, with appeals to the Higher Regional Court Stuttgart. Commercial register entries for companies seated in Stuttgart are kept by the local register court and are searchable free of charge through the joint register portal of the German states described on the Germany country page, including shareholder lists for GmbHs and filed articles.

Baden-Württemberg data protection

Federal data protection rules apply nationwide, but supervision of most private-sector processing is carried out at state level. For organisations established in Stuttgart this is the State Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information of Baden-Württemberg. Internal investigations at Stuttgart employers, many with strong works councils in the metal and electrical industries, should be planned with counsel, the data protection officer and works council arrangements in mind.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Stuttgart

For matters touching Stuttgart, TDSC starts by placing the companies involved in the regional automotive and engineering supply chain: which vehicle makers they depend on, who owns them, and whether they are in restructuring. Research draws on the commercial register, the company register for published accounts, insolvency announcements, court publications and German-language business media, reviewed under the GDPR and German data protection law. For disputes, work is aligned with German counsel and with the forum, including the English-capable Stuttgart Commercial Court where it applies. Where interviews or site inquiries in the Stuttgart region are needed, TDSC coordinates German professionals operating under the applicable trade rules. TDSC has no office in Stuttgart.

Questions

Stuttgart: Frequently Asked Questions

Which disputes can the Stuttgart Commercial Court hear?

The Commercial Court at the Higher Regional Court Stuttgart hears business-to-business company law disputes of at least 500,000 euros, including disputes over acquiring a company or at least 3 percent of its shares and claims between a company and its management or supervisory board. Proceedings may be in German or English. Counsel confirms whether a case qualifies.

Can TDSC assess the financial health of a Stuttgart supplier?

TDSC can analyse what is lawfully available: published annual accounts, commercial register changes, insolvency announcements, court records, ownership and management changes, and media reporting. Many smaller suppliers publish only abbreviated accounts, so TDSC reports the limits of the evidence and flags indicators of distress rather than presenting a definitive credit assessment.

Can TDSC investigate a suspected leak of engineering data?

TDSC can support counsel by researching corporate and professional links between departing employees, new companies and competitors, using registers and open sources. Any review of employee devices or communications is a matter for the employer and its counsel under German employee data protection law and works council rules; TDSC scopes its role accordingly.

Who supervises data protection for a Stuttgart employer?

Private-sector processing by organisations established in Stuttgart is generally supervised by the State Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information of Baden-Württemberg. TDSC limits personal data gathered to what the agreed purpose requires and plans any internal investigation work with the client's counsel and data protection officer.

Does TDSC have staff in Stuttgart?

No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Stuttgart or elsewhere in Germany. Engagements are scoped and managed from Nashville. Where a matter requires local inquiries, TDSC coordinates independent German investigators and works with the client's German counsel, within a written scope agreed before work starts.
